content.title: Collin Morikawa injury update after PGA Tour star withdrew from Players Championship
content.text: Morikawa is at home resting after withdrawing from the Players Championship -Credit:Getty Images (Getty Images)Collin Morikawa withdrew after playing just one hole at The Players Championship and is in rest mode now after suffering a back injury.Morikawa tweaked his back Friday on a practice swing and took himself out of contention for the $4.5 million purse at TPC Sawgrass following Rory McIlroy's withdraw from the Arnold Palmer Invitational where he also suffered an injury. An injury update was provided Friday, saying he is resting and preparing for future events.“He’s home,” said Kira Dixon on the Golf Channel broadcast. “Rest and recovery is a priority for Collin but it seems like all signs are pointing to his back injury being minor and it should not create further setbacks. Fingers crossed that we’ll see Morikawa back on the PGA Tour very soon as well.”• Incredible new images of $3.8 billion NFL stadium Donald Trump wants named after him• NFL team completes 'most consequential transaction in last five years' to land new QBMorikawa was coming off a top-five finish at the Arnold Palmer Invitational and had earned his first win in 849 days just weeks before that at the AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am."I felt fine in warm-up," Morikawa said. "Like nothing’s been any signs of back problems. Honestly, (on the) first hole (I) felt great, hit two great shots, hit a great putt. Teed it up, nothing felt bad. (I) teed it up on 11 and took one practice swing and I just knew it was gone. It all hit me at one second, where I was like, ‘Something doesn’t feel right.’""I took a practice swing, there it was, like not being able to swing. Trust me, I would play if I could. It’s just the worst thing in the world."Morikawa earned a win in the 2026 season at the AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am -Credit:Getty ImagesMorikawa initially thought it was just a muscle spasm.“I've had this stuff before, and been healthy all throughout the year, been moving weight and pushing, going fast,” said Morikawa.“I don't know, like, before I even took my practice swing, it's like you had, like a weird, like deja vu thing. I took the practice swing and immediately knew, like, I just couldn't get through impact. So at that point called over my trainer, and talked about it with my caddie Mark, and it just sucks. I don't know how to put it in words.”• Scottie Scheffler's brutal self-reflection speaks volumes after rough Players round• Angel Reese coach emerges as top candidate for Penn State jobHowever, Morikawa had no warning this injury was going to creep in.“No, no. I mean, warm-up, prep, nothing,” said Morikawa referring to if he could feel it before. “I was ready to go swing even harder this week if I had to, right. Honestly, first hole felt great. Hit two great shots. Hit a great putt. Teed it up, nothing felt bad. Honestly, it was like, it's like a deja vu. Like it all hit me at one second, where I was like, something doesn't feel right. I took a practice swing, there it was, like not being able to swing.”
